Created 2026-09-26. Owner: documentation and experiment-history agent; HPC
execution is coordinated by the root agent.

This file is the human-readable history for the active
[`latent pipeline`](04_latent_pipeline.md). It records what was configured,
executed, observed, failed, and decided. It must not turn a planned experiment
into a completed result or omit unsuccessful attempts.

## Separate Protenix attempt007 output policy passed; derivative gate failed, 23 October 2026

The [second collection](../outputs/hpc-submissions/source135-protenix-occupancy-native-attempt007-collect-002.json)
records **CPU 29796458 passed**, **128 fixtures**, zero failures/errors/skips
(6.18s), full gate **98.119s**, strict load, three preparations and successful
actual-input CPU feature preflight. The
[native result](../outputs/hpc-results/source135-protenix-occupancy-native-attempt007/snapshot-001/native/native-gate-result.json)
records **GPU 29796475 EXIT / exit 1**, **10:26:07–10:26:48 DTU-local** on
`n-62-18-5/gpua10`, 17 forwards/29.345s model phase, 38.026s controller phase.
Native repeat, FP32-boundary, C/Z and gradient-enabled q=1 comparisons passed
under declared finite/loss/TV acceptance. Original strict raw-logit failures
remain saved; this is not strict-logit parity.

The first [derivative row](../outputs/hpc-results/source135-protenix-occupancy-native-attempt007/snapshot-001/native/derivatives.jsonl)
is C q=0.1, direct-q parameterization: autograd **0**; FD at epsilon
**0.01 / 0.003 / 0.001** is **0 / -1.5141254176379941e-6 /
1.7269917995665907e-5**, with one pass and two failures. At least two agreeing
scales were required. Every difference was below the declared 10× repeat-delta
resolution threshold **2.405979715e-7**; sensitivity is `zero_or_unresolved`.
Scalar differences around `1e-8` are consistent with forward jitter; the single
repeat delta is not a rigorous noise bound. No incorrect-gradient or root-cause
conclusion is established. The unchanged derivative gate stopped before Z,
actual NO_ATOM-logit derivatives, sweeps and confirmation cases. No further
waiver or replacement submission is selected; no optimization/training ran.
The [30-file export receipt](../outputs/hpc-results/source135-protenix-occupancy-native-attempt007/snapshot-001/collection-receipt.json)
has SHA256 `8e4f87e8b69a7b11c2d2a21097beb6424746914e0e6e2cb92447752c44c4f797`.
All failed decisions, immutable bindings and unrelated chemistry records remain
preserved. [Exact results and limits](73_protenix_soft_occupancy_study.md#32-attempt007-output-policy-passed-first-control-derivative-gate-failed).

## Future best-trial optimization policy implemented; allocated checks pending, 18 October 2026

The user authorized a new future step policy, **`best_trial_v2`**, to attempt
the full requested update budget without an ordinary no-descent stall. Each
state tries the full proposed step and then progressive halves, accepting
the first actual strict scalar-loss decrease immediately. The default is
16 sizes `1, 1/2, ..., 2^-15`; the bounded trial count is configurable from
1 to 16. If none improves, choose the finite trial with lowest loss, even
when equal or worse than the current state, with earliest-trial tie breaking.
An equal/no-op finite update remains distinguishable from a strict improvement.
The state context, shared molecular mask, repaired target and coefficient stay
fixed throughout its trials. Armijo/ULP diagnostics do not add acceptance
requirements to v2. Consequently, future loss trajectories need not decrease
monotonically.

New receipts distinguish `acceptance_kind=first_improvement` from
`best_finite_fallback`, with a `monotone_descent` flag and separate applied,
improving, forced-fallback and no-op update counters. `accepted_updates` remains
a compatibility count of applied updates, not a descent certificate. Saved
best-observed state evidence carries its step/objective/context identity;
changing repaired-target totals are not one comparable ranking objective.
Metrics add `selection_reason`, `strictly_improved`,
`applied_loss_improvement` and `no_op`. Summary `best_binding_states` is keyed
by SHA256 of serialized JSON `[context_sha256, active_slots]`. Each value has
`step`, `loss`, `state_path`, `context_sha256`, `active_slots`,
`context_mask_sha256` and `scope`, with the ordinary saved scored state at
`best-binding-{key}.pt`. Only binding-only signed/scaled loss within the same
context/occupied-slot identity is ranked; no global changing repair-total
ranking is introduced.
All-nonfinite trials, native-gate failures, unexpected exceptions and resource
limits remain real failures/partial runs. A completed loop or configured
budget alone does not establish successful full-budget execution.

This is an explicitly changed future optimizer protocol. It does not authorize
rerunning or editing source120, changing its original frozen epoch 89 decoder,
initial latent/context, repair ramp or Armijo/trust/native scientific checks.
The healthy 225-accepted/226-attempted control stall remains a partial-budget
historical outcome; the sealed guided arm keeps its existing protocol. The
separate VAE chemistry continuation is unaffected. Explicit `armijo_v1`
compatibility remains required for historical replay, with no old record

The user requested conceptual investigation. [Docs45](45_dense_chemistry_100_epoch_continuation.md)
now distinguishes one-sided valence excess from absolute/signed-gap squared
penalties that would push implicit-hydrogen atoms toward maximum heavy-atom
valence. Squared positive excess is a separate possible loss but preserves
the carbon-to-sulfur cap shortcut. The preferred first prospective chemical
comparison is fixed-target repair NLL plus reconstruction/common anchors,

## Static host-RAM and sulfur-loss investigation, 10 October 2026

The user requested conceptual investigation, not implementation or training.
A100 80 GB denotes VRAM, separate from host RAM. Static reads of
[submit_decoder_density_long.py](../scripts/hpc/submit_decoder_density_long.py)
and [submit_defog_matched_pilot.py](../scripts/hpc/submit_defog_matched_pilot.py)
confirm GPU-stage requests of four cores × 16 GB per core = **64 GB host RAM**,
consistent with DTU's [resource](https://www.hpc.dtu.dk/?page_id=4976) and
[batch-job](https://www.hpc.dtu.dk/?page_id=1416) documentation. The current
all-record preparation/archive buffering and full-cache decompression can
scale host RAM with corpus size; peak at approximately 1.94 million molecules
is unmeasured. Batch-based GPU memory does not directly scale with total
corpus size. Chunked/sharded/memory-mapped data handling was suggested only.

Static loss review establishes a component-level escape route: with unchanged
bonds, occupancy and neutral charge, sulfur's maximum allowed valence 6
never has larger `E[max(V - cap, 0)]` than carbon's cap 4; at `V=5`, their
excesses are 0 and 1. This is an analytic property of the implemented proxy,
not a numerical test or a measured causal attribution of training drift.
[RDKit's allowed-valence documentation](https://www.rdkit.org/docs/RDKit_Book.html#valence-calculation-and-allowed-valences)
supports legitimate expanded sulfur valence; the incomplete maximum-valence
objective is not full validation. Existing occupancy/aromatic reference
anchors do not constrain prior element or charge identity. Undercoordination
cost zero accounts for implicit hydrogen; aromatic order one cannot enforce
ring/Kekulization consistency.

The existing [authenticated original metrics](../outputs/hpc-results/status-20261010-check002/original/metrics.json)
and [epoch-100 prior metrics](../outputs/hpc-results/status-20261010-check002/decoder/e100/prior/metrics.json)
confirm expected C/S counts 16.48/0.39 → 3.68/17.58 and size 22.09 → 22.07
over all 4,096 prior states, not only valid molecules. The [dated report](45_dense_chemistry_100_epoch_continuation.md)
separates these observations from the untested causal contribution of the
proxy. Candidate bond-focused stopped atom/charge gradients, identity-aware
bounded repair targets and a weak declared element/charge distribution trust
region remain unimplemented and unselected. Counterfactual/component-gradient
checks and legitimate sulfur examples are proposed before larger training;
none was executed and no validity or bias-removal guarantee is claimed.

The user asked whether approximately 1.94 million curated molecules would fit
HPC disk, what could be cleared, and whether chemistry guidance remains useful.

```powershell
ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 -o ConnectionAttempts=1 dtu-hpc "bash -lc 'timeout 45s du -x -B1 --max-depth=1 /work3/s234818/latentmol'"
```

Both exited 1. The first timed out during banner exchange to
`192.38.95.132:22`; the second timed out connecting to `login1.hpc.dtu.dk:22`.
The [last verified cleanup evidence](../outputs/hpc-results/hpc-space-cleanup-20261010-001.tar.gz)
remains the work3 quota at `2026-10-10T11:36:52+00:00`: **82.19/100 GiB used,
17.81 GiB free**, not a live capacity measurement. The same historical project
inventory reported data 12,660,736 bytes, releases 700,049,920 bytes, runs
35,875,124,736 bytes, cache 8,301,644,800 bytes and environment
8,326,721,536 bytes. No new cleanup candidates were authenticated; the unrelated
user project was not inspected or deleted. Earlier cleanup receipts remain
historical in [docs50](50_hpc_space_cleanup.md).

Static format arithmetic for 1,936,962 molecules at 50 slots gives 2,601
int8-label bytes per molecule (`50 atoms + 50 charges + 2,500 bonds + 1 split`),
about **4.69 GiB uncompressed**. Fixed-width Unicode SMILES add
`4 × molecule count × maximum SMILES length` bytes, about 0.72 GiB for a
100-character maximum. NPZ compression at this scale has not been measured.
Linear scaling of the existing 12.1 MiB directory from 229,694 molecules gives
roughly 102 MiB; this is an estimate, not preprocessing proof. Several GiB of
dataset space plus checkpoint/temp headroom looks feasible against the old
quota, but current free space cannot be certified. Preparation's all-record
stacking/BytesIO and the loader's full-cache decompression may require
substantial RAM independently of disk; neither path was exercised here.

Rule-based chemistry guidance remains an optional proposal, but the completed
decoder's sulfur drift requires revised penalties or composition monitoring
before a larger study can establish chemical utility. No coefficient, dataset
experiment or training design was selected in this review. No deletion,
download, preprocessing, numerical test, training, submission, scientific-code
change or VPN/SSH configuration change occurred.

## Decoder-only chemical-regularization protocol fixed, 7 October 2026 (pre-submission snapshot)

Protocol preparation now specifies the untouched source047 epoch-89 VAE plus
**six decoder-only fine-tuning cases**: seeds 17/23 × chemical coefficients
0/0.1/1, ten requested epochs each over all 215,000 training graphs. Encoder
parameters/buffers are frozen; new decoder-only AdamW uses learning rate
0.00003, batch 64, 16 normal-prior points per update, weight decay 0.00001 and
gradient cap 5. All arms share the original reconstruction loss **and
occupancy/aromatic KL anchors of weight one on prior points**. Thus the
alpha-zero comparator is reconstruction-plus-matched-anchors, not pure
original-loss continuation. Match data/order and posterior/prior/Monte Carlo
RNG within each training seed. **No new source/job, training pass/update or
quality improvement is claimed yet.**

The training chemistry term is a probability-aware **defect proxy**: exact
expected local valence excess under an explicit finite element/charge table,
normalized by 3 × max(expected occupancy, 1), unsupported charge mass and
empty risk, plus a four-draw global component-cost score-function estimator
with independent leave-one-out baselines. Local isolated-atom weight is zero.
AROMATIC contributes optimistic order one; undercoordination is unpenalized.
Apply chemistry equally to posterior and prior points (0.5 each). This is
not globally nearest-valid edit distance, a complete chemical validator or
a pathwise graph derivative. The separate bounded probability-repair search
evaluates the first 64 prescribed prior argmax outputs; it does not supply
the training gradient. Exact rules, anchors/estimator and limits are in
[docs39](39_decoder_chemical_distance_training.md).

Validation prior is 256/seed 81000; final prior is 4,096/seed 91000, each
argmax plus four categorical draws with no filtering. Final reconstruction
covers 7,347 protected test graphs. Engineering smoke is two epochs on
512 train/64 validation/32 prior points at alpha 0/1 with matched seed,
requiring finite/frozen/matched RNG/decoder-change evidence, **not** chemical
improvement. Planned long execution is one serial `gpul40s` 23-hour allocation
after CPU checks, controller 79,200 seconds, case cap 10,800 seconds with
budget reservation and explicit censoring. Exact source/config/script/resource
and submission receipts await implementation; all numerical work remains HPC.
Original checkpoint and prior molecular-optimization experiments are intact.

`src/latentmol/boltz/local_fd.py` declares the full plan before scoring any
perturbed endpoint. It requires the normalized-gradient direction plus
three Gaussian directions selected from at most 64 seeded proposals using
`abs(g dot d) >= 0.5 * norm(g) / sqrt(latent_numel)`. All considered
proposals, digests, projections, accepted/rejected decisions and reasons
are retained. Selection depends on the analytic projection only; a
direction is never replaced after seeing its finite differences. Pool
exhaustion fails. The legacy seeded direction is also measured and reported,
with endpoint reuse if it was selected, but it is explicitly **not required
for a new-policy pass**. Its original failure remains retained.

The predefined epsilon grid is `1e-5`, `3e-5`, `1e-4`, `3e-4`, `0.001`,
`0.003`, `0.01`, `0.03`, `0.1`. Each required direction needs at least two
**consecutive grid entries** that pass the original 5%/`1e-6` tolerance
and an additional informative-signal guard: projected derivative exceeds
the absolute tolerance, expected difference exceeds one output ULP, observed
endpoint difference is nonzero and the realized chord is nonzero. Nominal
finite differences determine the comparison; disclosed chord corrections
and widened diagnostic dot products do not manufacture passes. Output ULP
is scalar spacing, not a bound on whole-network numerical error. Frozen
scorer, objective, fixed mask/context and model dtype remain unchanged;
there is no derivative through selection or removed NO_ATOM logits.

## Fresh-native trajectory evaluation authorized, 6 October 2026

The user authorized implementation and HPC submission of the proposed
comprehensive first experiment: **ordinary fresh-native Boltz scoring at
predefined saved trajectory checkpoints**, including argmax graphs and a
fixed categorical-sample budget, multiple native-pose seeds, both affinity
heads and comparisons with the corresponding starts. The source056 random
study and source057 carbon/protein panel remain separate, unchanged queued
experiments. This follow-up evaluates saved candidates; it does not train
a model or alter either optimization trajectory.

native-pose/budget settings, input study scope and resource schedule are
not yet sealed. They must be fixed before native outcomes are observed;
invalid, unavailable and failed attempts remain explicit, without choosing
replacement candidates by relaxed or native score. Candidate, parent,
target/MSA, source/config and frozen-model identities must be verified.
The proposed pipeline and denominator requirements will be documented in
[docs32](32_fresh_native_trajectory_evaluation.md).

prediction or scientific result is established by this authorization
entry. Local editing/static review and packaging are allowed; numerical
fixtures and all real-model evaluation remain HPC work. Exact source/data
identities, executed commands, scheduler receipts and outcomes will be
appended only after verification.

**Candidate budgets selected before native outcomes:** the user chose
argmax evaluation across all declared runs with a detailed sampled subset.
The proposed source058 protocol fixes checkpoint states **0, 10, 25, 50,
75 and 100**, with native-pose seeds **17, 23 and 31**. Candidate selection
is by checkpoint/draw index, never by relaxed or native score:

| Parent scope | Selected hard draws at each checkpoint | Maximum candidate memberships |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Source057, all 100 target/length cases | Argmax | 600 |
| Source057, C8 and C13 for each of ten proteins | First four categorical draws, in addition to argmax above | 480 |
| Source055 completed full C13 run, both arms | Argmax plus all eight categorical draws | 108 |
| Source056, ten random starts and both declared arms | Argmax plus first four categorical draws | 600 |

The maximum is **1,788 candidate memberships × three pose seeds = 5,364
logical seed outcomes**, before missing/invalid/failed cases and identity
eligibility checks. Shared chemical identities and repeated states may
reuse native predictions under the same target/model/seed/budget; those
memberships are not 5,364 unique predictions or independent replicates.
The original random-draw denominator is ten, and an unattempted fixed
arm after active-arm failure remains unattempted rather than completed.

The declared native settings are 100 structure-diffusion steps with zero
structure recycling, 100 affinity-diffusion steps with native affinity
recycling 5, one sample each, `bf16-mixed`, MSA subsampling budget 128 and
no molecular-weight correction. This native recycling/context path differs
from the relaxed zero-recycle optimization proxy; score retention is a
combined hard-decoding/native-preprocessing/fresh-pose check, not an
isolated attribution of loss to one stage.

The initial resource plan is **one serial 23-hour GPU allocation after
source057 continuation job 29604187 ends**, with a finite prediction
budget and retained partial completion. A later boundary continuation
requires its own receipt under the same sealed identities. The maximum
logical-outcome count is not a guarantee all evaluations fit the first
allocation. Root implementation/config sealing are in progress; there is
still no source058 archive identity, passed fixture or submission receipt
at this protocol-choice snapshot.

affinity heads. No new connection, numerical test, source release, upload,
submission or chemical result is claimed by this planning entry.

carbon-chain lengths per protein**. The coordinator's provisional length

## Sequential ten-random-start study requested, 2 October 2026

The user requested **one long HPC job with ten sequential random latent
starts**, to compare final molecule diversity, atom-count changes and
carbon-chain initialization bias. The preparation plan uses exactly ten
unfiltered standard-normal `N(0, I)` draws with frozen VAE and Boltz
weights; seed failures remain in the original denominator. No redraw or
selection for validity/affinity is allowed. Paired active/fixed arms with
the same 100-update budget are intended, with exact seeds, source, count
support and allocation to be frozen before submission. The protocol draft
is [docs30](30_sequential_random_start_study.md).

This plan changes molecular latent initialization, while retaining possible
carbon-template **pose/context** bias. It does not replace or alter the
already submitted focused C13 job 29545141. At this snapshot there is no
new job, random-start numerical test or result. Local implementation and
review are in progress; an SSH attempt reached the DTU banner but aborted
before authentication. That access observation is not a job failure or
evidence that the existing C13 job stopped.

**Source056 implementation plan settled:** use integer seeds **0–9**, each
drawn once as float32 `N(0, I)` by an independently seeded CPU
`torch.Generator`, with width read from the frozen VAE (256). Per seed,
attempt active then fixed-initial-mask arms at 100 updates each, learning
rate `400`, gradient cap `0.000125`, trust radius `3`, temperature `1`
and occupancy threshold `0.5`. If the active arm aborts its pilot, the
fixed arm remains explicitly `not_attempted`; the study retains all ten
seed records rather than pretending ten paired successes occurred.

Prepare native counts **1–50** sequentially before optimization, reusing
verified counts 11–15, then seal a new catalog with all failures and actual
support retained. No clamping or redraw is allowed. The planned derivative
grid expands to `[0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1]`; tolerances remain
`0.05` relative / `1e-6` absolute with two passing scales per direction.
This changes probe-call budget relative to C13, not gate tolerance.

New modules separate start policy (`initialization.py`), subprocess handling
(`boltz/workflow_process.py`), serial study orchestration
(`boltz/random_start_study.py`) and artifact-only reporting
(`boltz/initialization_report.py`). A single 12-hour GPU allocation with
`ended(29545141)` dependency is proposed; source/config/schema hashes,
exact allocation and receipt are still forthcoming. No release is sealed,
no study job is submitted, and no numerical fixture/preparation/model test
has run at this implementation snapshot.

resume of either ten-update pilot. The source055 production code, frozen

`active_set` with `fixed_initial_mask` at matched budgets. Learning rate
`400` and a raw-gradient norm cap of `0.000125` bound each proposal's
displacement by `0.05` before trust-region projection. The trust radius is
**3.0**, widened from the pilots' `1.0`; this is a distinct, exploratory
optimization regime, not established latent-support coverage. Temperature
is `1`, the NO_ATOM selection threshold is `0.5`, and native contexts exist
only for counts **11–15**. Unsupported or empty selections stop the run;
there is no silent count clamp or fallback.

tolerances and the rule requiring two passing scales in each probe
direction. At each of 101 saved states, each arm produces one argmax and

## Source055 reruns completed, 2 October 2026

Both config-only reruns are **DONE**, including their separate fresh-native
pose follow-ups. Job **29544791**, learning rate `0.05`, ran
10:34:03–10:41:29 DTU local time (**446 seconds**). Job **29544792**,
learning rate `400`, ran 10:41:29–10:52:55 (**686 seconds**). These outcomes
supersede the RUN/PEND snapshots below; no new experiment was submitted for
this status check. The unchanged source055 archive/source, exact launcher,
config-file hashes, C13 start, source047 VAE checkpoint, frozen Boltz weights
and count-context catalog are identified in the investigation record below.

Both pilots passed their initial derivative gates, completed ten updates
per arm and recorded unchanged frozen weights. The original-learning-rate
baseline retained `CCCCCCCCCCCCC` as both argmax endpoints, with no relaxed
score change. Its downloaded fresh-rescore report confirms two successful,
identity-eligible native predictions and zero start/endpoint difference:
the start and endpoint are the same molecule.

The larger-step pilot changed both argmax endpoints to the RDKit-valid
`CCCCCCCCCC1CC1C`. Its relaxed binary-affinity score rose from
`0.0790553540` to `0.0887691677`, and final latent displacement was
`0.9857687354`. The trajectory was not monotonic: the score peaked near
`0.102040` at step 7, and the trust-radius boundary was reached at steps
7–9. Ten updates do not establish convergence. Each arm saved **99/99
valid hard candidates** across the eleven saved states, with five distinct
SMILES. These are correlated samples from this trajectory, not a general
validity estimate or 99 independent optimized molecules.

The larger-step fresh-pose follow-up completed **four native predictions**,
with no failures or identity-ineligible inputs. Binary scores increased
at both predeclared pose seeds:

| Pose seed | Start binary score | Endpoint binary score | Difference | Start continuous value | Endpoint continuous value |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 17 | 0.1153757274 | 0.1697086692 | +0.0543329418 | 1.5047349930 | 1.6598023176 |
| 23 | 0.1421509385 | 0.2255943418 | +0.0834434032 | 0.8483028412 | 1.4638851881 |

Only the **binary** head was optimized. The continuous head also increased;
this is not an improvement under its native `log10(IC50 in micromolar)`
interpretation, where lower values indicate stronger predicted activity
and intended comparisons are restricted to actives. The disagreement
between heads is a scientific limitation, not confirmation of better binding.

Both arms retained **13 atoms with zero context switches** and reached the
same endpoint. Their native predictions were shared/deduplicated, so the
two arms are not independent replications and establish no active-set
advantage or successful atom-count adaptation. This is one target/start
and two fresh Boltz pose seeds, using the same frozen model for optimization
and confirmation. There was no DeFoG/chemistry-prior branch, experimental
binding, synthesis or selectivity evaluation.

## Boltz active-set atom-count extension — design/implementation record, 1 October 2026

The user requested the simplest variable-count extension of the established
fixed-count Boltz gradient path. At each latent state, select slots whose
ordinary decoded `NO_ATOM` probability is strictly below `0.5`; within that
step, condition selected atom logits on real elements and use the existing
fixed-occupancy soft atom/charge/bond adapter. After an update to `z`, decode
again and allow a different slot mask or count at the next step. This is a
sequence of fixed-count differentiable steps separated by discrete context
selection, **not** a gradient through atom birth/death. The user requested no
occupancy-dependent gradient scaling in this first implementation.

The local source now adds
`python -m latentmol.boltz.prepare chain-count-example --output ... --count N`
for a separate carbon-chain native input/manifest per requested count;
the existing `snapshot --input-manifest ...` check binds a prepared tensor
context to that declared input. The check covers the cropped ligand,
declared YAML, target sequence/MSA file hashes and native record stem; it
does not independently prove the processed native protein/MSA tensors came
from those files. The `count-catalog` command indexes same-target/MSA,
hash-identified prepared count
snapshots and records source-manifest/source-archive identities and the HPC
job ID when available. The unexecuted
`scripts/hpc/boltz_active_set_prepare.sh NEW_ATTEMPT_DIR AE_CHECKPOINT COUNTS...`
would perform a separate short-budget native prediction, pose and tensor
snapshot for each count before writing that catalog. No helper invocation is
claimed.

The untested `src/latentmol/boltz/active_set.py` runner is configured by
`configs/boltz_active_set.example.yaml` and invoked as
`python -m latentmol.boltz.active_set --config CONFIG.yaml` in an immutable
HPC job; untested wrapper `scripts/hpc/boltz_active_set_run.sh
VERIFIED_CONFIG.yaml` supplies the same entrypoint in an allocation. The
config's required `mode: ae|vae` is checked against the decoder checkpoint.
It compares `active_set` against `fixed_initial_mask` from the
same encoded carbon-chain start, with matched optimizer steps. Before
loading Boltz, the encoded start must select **the exact anchor native slot
mask** at the `0.5` threshold and ordinary argmax must recover the full
prepared carbon-chain graph. A mismatch fails and is retained, even if a
different decoded count has its own prepared catalog entry. It rebinds
slots to native atom/token rows for same-count changes and selects another
prepared pose/features for a count change. The intended run artifacts are
per-arm `gates.json`, `transitions.jsonl`, `metrics-STEP.json`,
`state-STEP.pt`, `candidates.jsonl` and `summary.json`, plus run-level
`oracle_cost.json`/`summary.json`; the latter hashes both arm candidate
files. A missing selected count writes
`rejected-transition-STEP.json` with the requested mask/available counts
then fails. Verified decoder/Boltz asset loading occurs inside the recorded
run so loader failures are retained. The conditional finite-difference gate
holds the current mask fixed and records if the natural threshold selector
would cross under its perturbations. The code reports frozen-state identity
and labels fresh-native confirmation `required_not_run`; none of these
artifacts or checks exist as an executed result yet.

`tests/test_boltz_active_set.py` has been authored to check the selector's
threshold/tie rule, native slot rebinding, conditional `NO_ATOM` derivative,
fixed-control empty-selector diagnostic and native-rescore endpoint
selection. It has **not** been executed locally or on HPC, so it provides no
passing-test evidence.

The separate untested `src/latentmol/boltz/active_set_rescore.py` CLI is
`python -m latentmol.boltz.active_set_rescore --pilot RUN_DIR
--template NATIVE_INPUT_YAML --cache BOLTZ_CACHE --run-root RUNS`. It fixes
each arm's initial/final argmax endpoints before native calls, retains
invalid endpoints without repair, verifies the template target/MSA against
the count catalog, hashes both parent candidate files to lock selection
inputs, verifies the native affinity checkpoint matches optimization, and
resolves relative template MSA paths before native prediction. It
would use matched native pose seeds 17 and 23 for valid hard molecules.
No follow-up run, prediction or score retention is
claimed.

This record is a protocol/engineering task, **not an experiment result**.
There is no submitted HPC job, no local or HPC numerical test for this
extension, no prepared multi-count Boltz context set, no molecular trajectory
and no native rescore. Exact source/config/asset hashes and run artifacts
therefore remain unavailable. Later evidence must include per-count native
context preparation and identity, parity and finite-difference gates within
each mask, threshold/slot transition history, unsupported/failing states,
context-switch score jumps and fresh-native hard-candidate confirmation.
The method and its limits are described in
[`28_multimodel_experiments.md`](28_multimodel_experiments.md).

**Protocol steering, 1 October 2026 (no experiment ID):** docs26 now
requires graded closeness diagnostics for schema-supported pre-projection
candidates alongside binary final RDKit validity. Proposed measures are
atom/charge-aware local violation severity, fixed-alignment label-edit cost
to an actually reached valid projection at equal budgets (with bond counted
once and size/charge edits separate), valid fraction/captured mass by small
edit budget, and same-candidate property retention after repair and fresh
native rescore. Invalid, unsupported, unrepaired and censored attempts remain
visible; DeFoG is not assumed to be a projector or required for already
suitable candidates; already valid inputs have zero distance to validity,
with projector-induced changes reported separately. This is **protocol design only**: no new code, scorer
training, job or result is recorded by this steering.
An optional later alternating update is also proposed: detach a compatible
projector's corrected hard graph `H` and differentiate `-log q_z(H)` via
`sampling.hard_graph_log_prob` through the frozen decoder into `z`, subject
to schema/slot/occupancy support and a movement budget. This is not a
projector gradient or unbiased repair-process gradient; size-changing `H`
is incompatible with fixed-C13 Boltz. This differentiable fixed-target
surrogate is distinct from the proposed hard edit measurement; it remains
unimplemented and unrun.

**Graded-diagnostics implementation record, 1 October 2026 (no experiment
ID):** `src/latentmol/quality.py` now implements hard-graph RDKit problem
burden, connectedness, supplementary coverage-limited overvalence,
fixed-alignment label-edit cost for **supplied** repair outputs, and a
versioned configurable 0–100 heuristic chemistry summary. The default
weights are 0.4 validity, 0.4 local consistency and 0.2 connectedness;
any missing positive-weight component makes the combined score unavailable.
Repair uses an identified exact external budget and records censored
distance separately from zero observed utility; native retention remains
unavailable. The local evaluator now records per-attempt graded hard-graph
records and cohort summaries for reconstruction (within its chemistry
subset), neighborhood, VAE prior and fixed-`z` categorical/argmax arms;
standalone evaluation enables graded/raw-graph retention while reusable
training probes default those switches off. Both evaluator CLIs accept
custom score weights. The local `quality_panel.py` driver is prepared to
compare the source050 sealed 128-validation-index VAE/AE panel at 16
categorical draws per molecule on CPU, with separate argmax/categorical
reports and no projector/native-scorer calls. Its equal **evaluation**
budget does not erase unequal original training epochs. See
[docs27](27_graded_quality_diagnostics.md) for the API and artifact contract.
This is a local code/documentation state only: immutable release identity,
HPC tests and new molecular results have **not** yet been supplied or
claimed. It changes no optimization
objective and trains no scorer.

context skip, and one residual context block with two 96→96 linear layers.
The existing symmetric bond head and graph contract are intended to stay
fixed. The "520" wording
is provisionally interpreted as 512 based on the preceding "512 block"
description. The direct output projection is expected to exceed the previous
150% decoder-parameter cap, a user-directed exception for this candidate
only. Exact counts and numerical checks must come from HPC. Design and
comparison limits are in
[`24_atom_pair_decoder_comparison.md`](24_atom_pair_decoder_comparison.md).
At this ledger entry there is **no immutable source release, source/config
hash, dataset execution, LSF job, run directory or result** for this arm.
Existing source040/041 jobs remain separate and unchanged.

finite with maximum absolute values **3.53**, **5.08** and **4.67**.
Atom and charge logits remained finite but reached maximum absolute values
**2.56×10¹⁰** and **2.89×10¹⁰**; bond logits contained **1,965 NaNs**.

`decoder.bond_head.0` (`LayerNorm`): its input remained finite but reached
maximum absolute value **1.83×10²¹**, while its output contained
**132,048 NaNs**. Bond cross-entropy and total reconstruction loss were
NaN; KL remained finite at **138.87**. This supports severe activation
amplification within the decoder before the first observed NaNs, but does
**not** yet localize the origin of that amplification or establish a fix.

### Native charge-standardization diagnostic — 28 September 2026

A deterministic diagnostic on the **DTU HPC login node**, using installed
Boltz commit `b1ebfc46ecf57f5414e0d1a6f9027bbb122c53bc`, confirmed why the charged
tyrosine candidate and neutral baseline have identical native affinity outputs.
This was an HPC login diagnostic, **not an LSF job**.

The native affinity input path in `boltz.data.parse.schema` calls
`standardize(seq)` at approximately line 1242; its `standardize` implementation
around lines 1844–1859 uses ChEMBL `standardize_mol`. Direct invocation of that
installed function gave:

| Submitted SMILES | Standardized native affinity input |
|---|---|
| `NC(Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O` | `NC(Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O` |
| `NC(Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)[O-]` | `NC(Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O` |

The charged candidate **collapses to the neutral baseline before native affinity
scoring**; it is not a distinct native affinity candidate. This explains equal
native binary and continuous outputs at both seeds and identifies the earlier
fixed-context charge gain as nonpersistent under native preprocessing. It does
not establish how other charge states or molecules are standardized.
Source018 had already predicted the charged submitted SMILES; those actual
attempts remain in the original denominators and cost records. Report submitted
SMILES identities separately from standardized native identities.
The exact activated-environment command and two-line stdout are transcribed in
[the native report](13_native_rescore.md). The SSH diagnostic exited **0** in
**10.7 seconds**; no scheduler job was created.

## 2. Run identity and state

Each process creates a unique run directory using the implemented form:

```text
run_id: YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ_<name>_<8-hex-suffix>
```

Link related run IDs as attempts of the same logical comparison in this ledger.
A scheduler resubmission or resumed process receives a new attempt record even
if it belongs to the same comparison. A single scheduler job may create multiple
run directories, such as tests followed by preprocessing. Array index and job ID
are separate fields. Never reuse an output directory in a way that erases a
failed attempt's evidence.

Allowed states:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Planned | Design exists; no submission confirmed |
| Prepared | Input/config artifacts recorded; not yet submitted |
| Submitted | Scheduler accepted submission; job ID recorded |
| Queued | Scheduler reports waiting for resources |
| Running | Scheduler or process evidence confirms execution |
| Completed | Process completed and required artifacts/results were inspected |
| Failed | Execution or a required check failed; error recorded |
| Cancelled | Deliberately stopped; actor/reason recorded |
| Interrupted | Terminated before a classified outcome, such as walltime or node loss |
| Unknown | Current status cannot be verified; last observation preserved |
| Superseded | Retained for history; replaced by a named run or corrected interpretation |

Use UTC timestamps for machine records, with explicit offsets if another time
zone is displayed. Record when a status was observed, not only when the process
was presumed to have changed state. Scheduler state and scientific acceptance
are separate: a completed job can produce an unacceptable model.

### Implemented Boltz adapter scope, without runtime evidence

The helper reports modules under `src/latentmol/boltz/{contracts,adapter,model}`.
`PreparedComplex` holds a tensor feature snapshot, detached `[1,1,A,3]` pose,
immutable decoder-slot to Boltz-atom/token mappings, the seed graph and provenance.
`fixed_occupancy_graph` conditions decoder logits on a fixed occupied-slot set;
there are no atom-count derivatives. `adapt_graph` changes soft `ref_element`
features `[1,A,128]`, expected scalar `ref_charge`, `token_bonds` as probability
of any bond, and expected typed-bond embeddings using native IDs `0/2/3/4/5`.

`FrozenBoltzAffinity` uses explicit official input-embedding, trunk and affinity
head modules with frozen parameters in evaluation mode while retaining chemical
input gradients. Geometry, crop/masks/pooling, atom names, reference conformer,
MSA/token metadata and pose stay fixed. Diffusion/confidence derivatives are
excluded, and affinity distances remain hard-binned. The output is the raw
uncorrected affinity head/ensemble probability with molecular-weight correction
disabled.

Planned hard-input parity means the native discrete trunk and affinity heads
at the **same fixed pose and recycle count**, not equality with a separate
stochastic full-diffusion prediction. No forward parity, finite-gradient,
directional finite-difference or latent-optimization result has yet passed.
The planned scope does not establish variable atom-count optimization through
Boltz, and these in-progress files are excluded from source-005.

| LR by stage | Epochs 1–60: 0.001; 61–80: 0.0003; 81–100: 0.0001; 101–120: 0.00003 |
| Continuation | Model-specific recent 10 versus prior 10 epochs: >=0.5% relative full-val reconstruction gain OR +1pp valid OR +0.5pp exact; validation only |
| Per-epoch diagnostics | Deterministic-mean train/val probes 2,048 each, full-val reconstruction, seeded 1,024-molecule validation chemistry |
| Full chemistry / stage-end diagnostics | Full validation chemistry every 10 epochs and phase boundary; stage-end VAE prior 1,024 and local neighborhoods 256 |
| Checkpoints | Every 10 global epochs plus selected/phase epochs; best loss, best validity and last. Validity ties use exactness then lower full-val loss; complete ties keep earlier epoch |
| Test policy | Both configs/rules fixed before launch; each model seals its decisions/selection before its test. Early test outcomes never alter either model; compare after both finish |
| Resumption | Source015 actual CUDA AE/VAE exact-resume checks passed for workers zero and one. Same-process automatic phases; scheduler recovery manual from explicit checkpoint |
| Source/config/cache identities | Sources011–014 hashes recorded; full-cache hashes, isolation and prior memberships verified; initialization hash comparison awaits artifacts |
| Jobs/attempts/results | Source014 failures retained; source015 validation/audit DONE; both initial 60-epoch phases complete, current phases RUN at epochs 77/76; test unopened |

The expected eligible total is from the prior audit, not a new manifest. Preserve
the earlier rejection/duplicate counts and report any differences. Do not reuse

## 4. Required record for each run

Each run has a structured manifest saved with its artifacts and a concise entry
here. Large per-step data belongs in the artifact files, not this Markdown file.

### Identity and purpose

- Run ID, attempt ID, stage, hypothesis and comparison group.
- Parent/checkpoint/resume run, if any; reason for rerun or restart.
- Creation, submission, start, end and last-observed timestamps as available.
- Owner/coordinator and actual command/entrypoint with arguments.

### Source and environment

- Repository commit hash, branch/reference for context, and working-tree state.
- If uncommitted code is executed, save the exact patch or source snapshot and
  its hash; a base commit alone does not identify the executed program.
- Hash of the resolved configuration and of the copied configuration file.
- Python, PyTorch, CUDA/runtime, driver and chemistry-library versions; additional
  model dependencies and environment lock/export path as relevant.
- Machine architecture, requested queue/GPU/CPU/RAM/walltime, allocated host/GPU,
  and observed runtime/peak memory when available.
- DTU HPC job ID, array index, scheduler status/exit reason, and stdout/stderr paths.

### Data and randomness

- Dataset source/version/license metadata and raw-data hashes or immutable IDs.
- Preprocessing configuration/code hash; processed dataset and split hashes.
- Ordered element, charge and bond vocabularies; `N_max`; chemistry/ordering rules.
- Total source/retained/excluded counts, with explicit exclusion reasons.
- Python/NumPy/PyTorch/CUDA seeds and split, dataloader, sampling, initialization
  or optimization seeds as applicable.
- Determinism settings and any known nondeterministic kernels or operations.

### Model, optimization and outputs

- Architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, schedules, batch size,
  gradient accumulation, precision and effective update count.
- Loss component definitions, weights and normalization/reduction rules.
- Checkpoint selection rule, selected epoch/step and evaluation decode policy.
- Input checkpoint paths and hashes; output checkpoint paths and hashes.
- For VAE: prior, posterior parameterization, KL coefficient/schedule and
  posterior-mean versus sampled evaluation policy.
- For Boltz2: source commit, weights hash, protein/target inputs, ligand adapter
  revision, fixed versus rebuilt features, gradient settings and objective terms.
- Metrics table/trajectory paths, summary report, candidate records and error logs.
- Actual result, limitations, acceptance decision and next action.

Use SHA-256 for file/config/source snapshot hashes unless the implementation
adopts and records another algorithm. A Git commit hash and a SHA-256 file hash
identify different things; retain both where relevant. Credentials, access
tokens, SSH private keys and environment secrets must never enter manifests or
logs.

## 5. Proposed artifact layout

The verified run root is `/work3/s234818/latentmol/runs`. Current code creates
one directory per process run with these actual filenames:

```text
/work3/s234818/latentmol/runs/<run_id>/
  run.json                     # config, provenance, timestamps and status
  metrics.jsonl                # append-only metric events
  command.log                  # combined output for generic wrapped commands
  traceback.txt                # if an ordinary exception is caught
  best.pt                      # training only
  last.pt                      # training only
  summary.json                 # evaluation only
  examples.json                # raw reconstruction examples
  neighbors.json               # raw latent-neighborhood examples
```

This list describes implemented outputs; retrieved evidence and available
training/evaluation artifacts are identified by run in the index above.
Scheduler stdout/stderr and JUnit reports live in the separate project `logs/`
directory; source releases live in `releases/`; a prepared cache contains
`dataset.npz` and `manifest.json`. Additional latent-optimization trajectories
are future artifacts. Preserve large artifacts on HPC and identify them by
exact path/hash; do not commit weights or datasets merely to establish provenance.

## 6. Metric definitions and reporting rules

State denominators and decoding policies next to results. Retain failures and
invalid candidates in the primary attempt count.

| Metric | Required definition / caveat |
|---|---|
| Codec round-trip success | Molecular identity under the declared normalization/stereochemistry policy, over attempted retained records |
| Exact reconstruction | Same molecular identity as the target after declared decoding; distinguish raw and repaired outputs |
| Atom / bond accuracy | State inclusion of padding and `NONE` bonds; also report occupied-atom / present-bond subsets |
| Charge accuracy/error | State scalar rounding or categorical decoding; include the relevant atom denominator |
| Raw validity | Named sanitization/connectivity requirements over all raw decoded candidates |
| Repaired validity | Separate metric with repair method, failure count and amount of change |
| Atom-count error | Predicted discrete count versus target; also report relaxed expected count when applicable |
| Uniqueness / novelty | Declared molecular identity policy, duplicate handling and reference dataset |
| VAE KL and latent use | Aggregation and posterior policy; low KL alone is not evidence of a useful prior |
| Relaxed objective | Every raw component plus weighted total, with score direction |
| Discrete reevaluation | Same scorer with ordinary discrete inputs and a declared feature-rebuilding policy |
| Independent evaluation | Evaluator version and confirmation it was excluded from optimization/selection as claimed |
| Valid candidate yield | Count satisfying stated criteria divided by all attempted trajectories or candidates |
| Compute | Updates, wall time, GPU time and actual resources where available |

For trajectory comparisons, retain each checkpoint's step number, elapsed time,
latent state identifier, decoder temperature, expected/discrete size, raw validity,
repair/projection status, and relaxed/discrete scores. A score missing because a
molecule is invalid is missing with an explicit reason, not a zero or silently
dropped row.

```text
incident_id:
run_id / attempt_id / scheduler_job_id:
first_observed_utc:
phase: setup | data | tests | training | evaluation | integration | optimization
symptom and exact error excerpt:
full log path and hash:

diagnosis: confirmed | suspected | unresolved
cause and supporting evidence:

resolution and confirming check:
```

Preserve the original failure before retrying. Do not turn a suspected diagnosis
into a confirmed cause because a later run happened to succeed. If a data or code
bug invalidates earlier metrics, mark the affected results invalid/superseded and
link the correction; retain the original record for auditability.

## 9. Update protocol

The execution coordinator sends the documentation owner the run identity,
resolved configuration/path, exact source identity, scheduler ID, current status,
and output/log locations. On completion or failure, it supplies the observed
metrics or error evidence and the acceptance decision.

The documentation owner updates the run index, decision register and concise
per-run summary, flags missing provenance, and checks that conclusions match the
reported evidence. The owner does not submit jobs or infer results from expected
behavior. Preserve explicit TBD/unknown states until the relevant observation or
decision is available.

## Verified CPU repair-gradient result and runtime-budget risk, 7 October 2026

Source072 actual-checkpoint job **29623958 completed**, wrapper return code 0;
started `2026-10-07T14:31:10.879391+00:00`, finished
`2026-10-07T14:44:21.217192+00:00`. The unchanged source/config/checkpoint
identities and exact numerical command/environment are retained in the source072
entries and downloaded wrapper/receipts. All numerical work ran on DTU HPC.
The actual frozen FP32 CPU VAE supplied 90 accepted valid-repair targets from
256 prescribed random latent points; 162 searches were censored and four raw
outputs were already valid. On the first accepted latent (ID 3), fixed-target
NLL autograd agreed with finite differences in both declared directions at
neighboring epsilons 0.003 and 0.001. Coarse epsilon 0.01 did not pass.
This verifies that surrogate gradient on one actual example, not improved
molecular generation, an exact nearest-valid distance, or CUDA training.
